title.narrative: Job Creation through Youth and Women-led Micro and Small Enterprises (JMSE)

description.narrative: The Project development objective is to strengthen the enabling environment for private sector growth and job creation.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

title.narrative: Staff of MoTI sponsored for capacity building (30% women)

description.narrative: An official and up-to-date register of staff members who have received project sponsorship or support, including scholarships, training sponsorships, internships, professional development opportunities, study tours, or other project-funded capacity-building interventions. The list should contain details such as participant names, gender, position, institution, type of sponsorship, duration, and status of completion

Photographic evidence documenting the successful installation, operational status, and location of equipment procured and installed under the project. The photographs should clearly show the equipment in its installed setting and, where applicable, demonstrate its use by beneficiaries or operating institutions. Photos should be dated, geo-referenced where feasible, and accompanied by installation reports or handover certificates to verify completion.

title.narrative: MoTI provided with a licenced financial software

description.narrative: This indicator measures the acquisition, installation, licensing, and operational use of a financial management software system by the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI) with support from the project. The software is intended to strengthen financial management, budgeting, accounting, reporting, internal controls, and financial data management within the ministry.

title.narrative: PSD strategy, National Export Strategy, and Trade Policy reviewed/revised

description.narrative: This indicator measures the completion of the review and/or revision of key national policy and strategic frameworks, namely the Private Sector Development (PSD) Strategy, National Export Strategy, and Trade Policy. The review process includes assessment of the existing frameworks, stakeholder consultations, identification of gaps and emerging priorities, drafting of revisions, validation, and formal submission or approval by the relevant government authorities.

title.narrative: Labour Market Analysis, Agriculture Value Chain study and tracer study carried out

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of key analytical studies completed under the project, specifically: (i) Labour Market Analysis, (ii) Agriculture Value Chain Study, and (iii) Tracer Study. The studies are undertaken to generate evidence for project design, implementation, monitoring, and decision-making, and to improve the relevance and effectiveness of interventions targeting employment, skills development, entrepreneurship, and agricultural market systems.

title.narrative: Number of registered MSEs linked to digital trade and markets (50% women)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of micro and small enterprises (MSEs) that are successfully registered and have active profiles on the existing trade portal managed by the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI) as a result of project support. Registration on the portal enables enterprises to increase their visibility, access market information, connect with buyers and suppliers, participate in trade opportunities, and enhance their digital presence within national and regional markets.

title.narrative: Youth and women-led MSEs with increased revenue (50% women)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of project-supported youth- and women-led micro and small enterprises (MSEs) that demonstrate an increase in business revenue compared to their baseline revenue levels. Revenue refers to the total income generated from the sale of goods and/or services over a specified reporting period. An enterprise is counted under this indicator when it records a measurable increase in revenue attributable, at least in part, to project-supported interventions such as access to finance, business development services, skills training, market linkages, technology adoption, or enterprise expansion.

This indicator measures the provision, installation, and operationalization of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) equipment to the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI) to strengthen institutional capacity, improve service delivery, enhance data management, support digitalization initiatives, and facilitate implementation of trade and private sector development programs.

This indicator measures the establishment and operationalization of a financing facility designed to improve access to finance for targeted beneficiaries, including youth- and women-led micro and small enterprises (MSEs), producer groups, cooperatives, or other eligible beneficiaries under the project. The financing facility may take the form of a revolving fund, credit facility, matching grant scheme, guarantee mechanism, interest-free loan fund, or other project-approved financial instrument.

title.narrative: Communication Plan developed and implemented; and transition Strategy of the financing facility developed.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the development, approval, and implementation of a project Communication Plan and the development of a Transition Strategy for the financing facility established under the project. The Communication Plan outlines the project's communication objectives, target audiences, key messages, communication channels, stakeholder engagement approaches, and implementation arrangements. The Transition Strategy provides a roadmap for the long-term sustainability, governance, management, and operational continuity of the financing facility beyond the project period.

title.narrative: Youth and women trained in business development, financial literacy and entrepreneurship (50% women)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of youth and women who successfully complete project-supported training programs in business development, financial literacy, and entrepreneurship. The training may cover topics such as business planning, enterprise management, financial management, budgeting, savings and investment, bookkeeping, marketing, digital business skills, access to finance, business formalization, and entrepreneurial mindset development.

title.narrative: Youth and women-led MSEs accessing interest free loans (50% women)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of youth- and women-led micro and small enterprises (MSEs) that successfully access interest-free loans through project-supported financing mechanisms during the reporting period. Interest-free loans refer to loans provided without interest charges and may be delivered through revolving funds, Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), microfinance initiatives, Islamic finance arrangements, government-supported financing schemes, or other project-approved financing facilities.

title.narrative: Direct jobs created by youth and women-led MSEs (50% women)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of direct employment opportunities created by youth- and women-led micro and small enterprises (MSEs) supported through the project. Direct jobs refer to paid or self-employment positions generated within the supported enterprises as a result of business establishment, expansion, or increased productivity. The indicator includes both full-time and part-time jobs that are sustained for a minimum period defined by the project (e.g., three months or more).

This indicator measures the number of formal or informal business-to-business (B2B) partnerships, commercial relationships, or market linkages established as a result of project interventions. These linkages may include supply agreements, distribution arrangements, subcontracting relationships, buyer-seller contracts, joint ventures, strategic partnerships, market access agreements, or other forms of commercial collaboration between enterprises.

title.narrative: New Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) established and registered

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of new Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) established and formally registered during the project implementation period with support from the project. A VSLA is considered established when a group of members has been mobilized, trained, constituted according to agreed governance structures, and has commenced savings and lending activities. A VSLA is considered registered when it has completed registration or recognition procedures with the relevant local authority, community institution, cooperative agency, or other legally recognized registration body, as applicable within the country context.
